### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. severe neurodegenerative syndrome with lipodystrophy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.776)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15832)

**Proposed mechanism:** BSCL2 (HGNC:15832) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid droplet formation and maintenance (GO:0006631); Lipid droplet formation and maintenance (GO:0006631) —LEADS_TO→ Seckel syndrome (HP:0001749); Lipid droplet formation and maintenance (GO:0006631) —LEADS_TO→ Lipodystrophy (HP:0009071). Loss-of-function mutations in BSCL2 disrupt its role in lipid droplet formation and maintenance, leading to the shared phenotypes of Seckel syndrome and lipodystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in BSCL2 leading to a gain-of-function mechanism for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a pathogenic variant in BSCL2 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 would also challenge the rare disease classification.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of BSCL2 in lipid metabolism and its downstream effects on cellular homeostasis could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both rare diseases by targeting lipid droplet dynamics or related pathways.

---

#### 2. neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, type 5C  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.772)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15832)

**Proposed mechanism:** BSCL2 (HGNC:15832) —DISRUPTS→ Seipin function in lipid droplet formation and ER membrane homeostasis (GO:0005833); Seipin function in lipid droplet formation and ER membrane homeostasis (GO:0005833) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007314); Seipin function in lipid droplet formation and ER membrane homeostasis (GO:0005833) —LEADS_TO→ Distal muscle weakness (HP:0002460). Loss-of-function mutations in BSCL2 disrupt its function in lipid droplet formation and ER membrane homeostasis, leading to both motor neuron degeneration (MONDO:0010043) and distal muscle weakness (MONDO:0030860).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in BSCL2 who exhibit phenotypes entirely unrelated to motor neuron degeneration or lipid metabolism, or conversely, individuals with MONDO:0010043 or MONDO:0030860 without any BSCL2 variants. _(variant: gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/11-69097913-C-A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BSCL2 in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting lipid droplet homeostasis or ER membrane integrity that benefit patients with either condition.

#### 3. congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15832)

**Proposed mechanism:** BSCL2 (HGNC:15832) —DISRUPTS→ Seipin function in ER membrane dynamics and lipid droplet formation (GO:0005886); Seipin function in ER membrane dynamics and lipid droplet formation (GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital generalized lipodystrophy (HP:0000027); Seipin function in ER membrane dynamics and lipid droplet formation (GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ Seckel syndrome (HP:0001332). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in BSCL2 that lead to a gain-of-function mechanism for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, the discovery of distinct causal genes for each disease that do not interact with BSCL2 or its downstream pathways would also falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs757058884 (c.470C>T, p.Ala157Val) is a common variant in gnomAD with an allele frequency > 0.01, suggesting it is likely benign and not the causal variant for these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BSCL2 in lipid metabolism and cellular structure could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting shared pathways for both lipodystrophy and Seckel syndrome.
